body:
Geometry is everywhere: in a window frame, a pizza slice and the letters on this page.

The parts:
- A point is an exact location.
- A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. A line goes on forever in both directions.
- An angle is made by two rays that share an endpoint.

Angles are measured in degrees. A full turn is 360 degrees, and a quarter turn, a right angle, is 90 degrees. An acute angle is less than 90 degrees, and an obtuse angle is between 90 and 180 degrees.

Parallel lines never meet. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.

In this unit we use a protractor, sort shapes by their sides and angles, and fold shapes to find lines of symmetry.
title: The Geometry Around Us
